paragraphs: Understanding an advertisement requires connecting visible events to the persuasive message behind them. AD-MIR addresses this gap with a two-stage system that first organizes video evidence and then reasons about marketing intent. Its design makes details such as branding and on-screen text part of the reasoning process.

The first stage constructs a structured memory using both semantic retrieval and exact keyword matching. It emphasizes fine-grained brand information while filtering irrelevant background content and identifying key protagonists. The second stage repeatedly asks questions about the narrative to infer persuasion tactics. It checks those interpretations against particular video frames and backtracks when the visual evidence does not support them.

On AdsQA, AD-MIR reports state-of-the-art results, exceeding the general-purpose agent DVD by 1.8 percentage points in strict accuracy and 9.5 points in relaxed accuracy. These findings support the value of combining structured video memory with explicit evidence checking when interpreting abstract advertising strategies.
icml-2026-ad-mir-bridging-the-gap-from-p.tldr: AD-MIR interprets advertising strategies through structured video memory and reasoning that checks its conclusions against specific frames.

paragraphs: When a student language model learns from a teacher model’s outputs, the teacher’s owner may want to detect that training relationship. Existing fingerprinting approaches alter generated text to leave recognizable traces, but stronger traces can come at a substantial cost to the usefulness of the teacher’s responses.

Antidistillation fingerprinting selects those alterations with the student’s learning process in mind. It builds on a gradient-based sampling framework and uses a proxy model to identify tokens expected to make the fingerprint more detectable after student fine-tuning. The central change is to optimize for what training will leave inside the student, rather than simply introduce biases and hope they survive.

Experiments on GSM8K, OASST1, and MBPP cover mathematical reasoning, dialogue, and code generation. The authors report a better trade-off between detection confidence and utility than leading baselines, including when the student architecture is unknown. The findings suggest that modeling fingerprint absorption can improve attribution without imposing the same degree of output degradation.
icml-2026-antidistillation-fingerprintin.tldr: Antidistillation fingerprinting chooses teacher outputs to make subsequent student training more detectable while minimally affecting usefulness.

paragraphs: Synthetic-image detectors can learn the particular fake patterns present during training and then struggle with unfamiliar ones. BPL approaches this problem by focusing on relationships between real and synthetic images that share semantic content. Such relationships can reveal changes introduced by generation that treating each image independently may overlook.

The framework constructs real–fake pairs using source information or nearby representations in CLIP’s embedding space. It learns to enlarge the discrepancies associated with generation and introduces discrepancy inversion to reduce overfitting. This puts the comparison between related images at the center of detector training, rather than relying only on separate real-or-fake labels.

BPL also updates only model biases during fine-tuning. Restricting adaptation in this way is intended to preserve pretrained semantic representations while limiting the capacity to memorize familiar fake patterns. Experiments report stronger generalization to unseen fake patterns. Together, the results support combining pair-based training with restrained adaptation to improve detection beyond the synthetic examples encountered during training.
icml-2026-bpl-generalizable-deepfake-det.tldr: BPL combines comparisons of related real–fake image pairs with bias-only fine-tuning to improve detection of unfamiliar synthetic patterns.

paragraphs: Choosing training data involves more than deciding how much to sample from each source. This paper argues that training examples can influence one another directionally, making their order consequential. Learning from an influential training unit earlier may change how effectively the model learns from other units later.

D³ represents these relationships as a changing directed graph. Its edges describe dependencies measured through loss, and a constrained optimization procedure uses the graph to determine training order. Because the graph evolves during learning, the schedule can reflect changes in the relationships between training units instead of following one fixed ordering throughout.

The authors provide theoretical motivation and report consistent improvements over existing scheduling approaches during both pre-training and post-training. They also introduce an approximation algorithm to keep the additional computation manageable. The contribution is therefore a way to make interactions among training units operational: those interactions guide sequencing, while the approximation addresses the cost of applying that idea at scale.
icml-2026-d-3-dynamic-directional-graph-.tldr: D³ schedules language-model training using a dynamic directed graph of loss-based dependencies between training units.

paragraphs: A multimodal model can give the right answer while selecting the wrong visual evidence to support it. DeFacto targets this mismatch by training models to align their answers with relevant image content. The goal is to improve both answer correctness and the consistency of the evidence behind the answer.

Its training combines positive examples, counterfactual examples, and random masking. A language-guided construction pipeline identifies image regions relevant to a question and creates counterfactual variants, producing DeFacto-100K. Models then undergo GRPO-based reinforcement learning with three rewards that separately encourage correct answers, structured reasoning, and consistent evidence selection.

The authors also introduce DeFacto-1.5K, a human-annotated benchmark designed to assess evidence–answer consistency beyond answer accuracy alone. Experiments across diverse benchmarks report substantial improvements on both measures over strong baselines. This combination of training data, rewards, and evaluation makes visual support an explicit target of learning and measurement, rather than treating a correct final answer as sufficient evidence of faithful reasoning.
icml-2026-defacto-counterfactual-thinkin.tldr: DeFacto uses counterfactual image training and evidence-focused rewards to improve both answer accuracy and visual evidence consistency.

paragraphs: Source-free domain adaptation adjusts an existing model to a changed data distribution without revisiting its original training data. This paper studies regression, where predictions lie on an ordered, continuous scale. That structure makes adapting representations and refining model-generated training targets different from the corresponding problems in classification.

The proposed algorithm uses discretized density information to guide the refinement of pseudo-labels. Its supervisory signals depend on individual examples and account for uncertainty, rather than treating every predicted target as equally dependable. An auxiliary task learns a discretized distribution and encourages the model’s internal features to become more compact and structured.

The authors theoretically show that the resulting density structure is robust to potential perturbations and report effective adaptation across multiple benchmarks. The approach connects two parts of the problem: improving the provisional labels used for adaptation and organizing the representations that produce them. Its source-free setting is particularly relevant when access to the original data is restricted for privacy reasons.
icml-2026-discretized-density-guided-sou.tldr: The method adapts regression models without source data by using uncertainty-aware, discretized density signals to refine pseudo-labels and representations.

paragraphs: Converting a trained artificial neural network into a spiking neural network can avoid another expensive training process. That possibility is attractive for reinforcement learning, where gathering experience can be costly or unsafe. However, the paper finds that existing conversion methods struggle when the resulting network must produce continuous control actions.

The identified problem is error amplification across decisions. Small errors in approximating actions become correlated over time, changing the states the controller encounters and progressively damaging performance. CRPI addresses this by carrying residual membrane potentials across decision steps. This lightweight, gradient-free mechanism is designed to suppress the temporal correlations that allow small conversion errors to accumulate.

Experiments with both vector and visual observations show that CRPI can fit into existing conversion pipelines and substantially recover lost performance. The findings make continuous control an informative test of conversion quality: preserving individual outputs approximately can still leave harmful errors across a sequence of interacting decisions. CRPI targets that sequential failure directly.
icml-2026-error-amplification-limits-ann.tldr: CRPI carries residual membrane potentials across control steps to reduce error amplification when converting trained networks into spiking networks.

paragraphs: This paper studies online reinforcement learning with a fixed terminal time in a non-episodic setting. Estimating returns all the way to that endpoint is challenging, and methods developed for infinite horizons do not naturally capture this structure. The authors instead define an action-value function that looks ahead only K steps.

Their tabular algorithm combines this shorter planning objective with a changing threshold: an action is selected only when its estimated lookahead value exceeds that threshold. The authors prove fast finite-sample convergence, including minimax-optimal constant regret for K equal to one and a separate regret bound for longer lookahead. These guarantees concern the proposed objective.

The experimental implementation increases K over time to balance planning depth against estimation variance. Evaluations on synthetic decision processes, JumpRiverswim, FrozenLake, and AnyTrading report higher cumulative rewards than leading tabular methods. The findings suggest that adapting how far ahead the learner plans can improve practical reward collection while retaining a theoretically analyzed learning procedure.
icml-2026-fast-non-episodic-finite-horiz.tldr: A tabular reinforcement-learning method combines K-step planning with time-varying action thresholds and adaptively deepens lookahead during evaluation.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts training must develop expert weights while also learning which experts should process inputs. Grouter addresses the slow convergence and instability associated with searching for that routing structure at the same time as updating the experts. It supplies routing information obtained from already trained mixture-of-experts models.

The method distills those learned structures into a router that remains fixed for a target model. Expert folding adapts the router to different model configurations, while expert tuning rebalances workloads when the data distribution changes. The resulting routing structure also enables targeted optimizations intended to increase training throughput.

Experiments report improved performance and efficiency, including 4.28 times better pre-training data utilization and throughput acceleration of up to 33.5%. These are distinct benefits: learning can make better use of training data, and the training system can process work faster. The contribution is an approach to reusing learned routing structure so that target-model training need not jointly discover that structure and learn expert representations.
icml-2026-grouter-decoupling-routing-fro.tldr: Grouter transfers routing structures from trained mixture-of-experts models to accelerate target-model learning and throughput.

paragraphs: This paper addresses an encoding problem relevant to visual prostheses: generating M/EEG brain signals from images. It complements work on decoding visual information from brain signals by studying the conversion in the other direction. The proposed framework uses a diffusion transformer to generate signals conditioned on image information.

Cross-attention connects brain-signal representations with CLIP image embeddings. To add semantic guidance, a language model produces image captions, whose CLIP text embeddings are combined with the image embeddings. A learnable position encoding incorporates both brain-region information and time, allowing the generator to represent where and when signal patterns occur.

The diffusion process is based on denoising diffusion implicit models, and the framework is evaluated on THINGS-EEG2 and THINGS-MEG. The authors report biologically plausible generated signals on these benchmarks. The demonstrated contribution is therefore an image-conditioned brain-signal generator that combines semantic guidance with spatial and temporal structure, addressing an encoding component of the broader visual-prosthesis pipeline.
icml-2026-image-to-brain-signal-generati.tldr: A diffusion transformer combines CLIP image and caption representations with spatial and temporal encoding to generate plausible M/EEG signals.

paragraphs: Notification systems must choose both when to send a message and how to present it, while respecting operational limits. This paper treats each combination as a bundle and aims to maximize incremental daily active users. The optimization includes a platform-wide budget and quotas associated with different device vendors.

BUOPLR separates estimating a bundle’s effects from deciding which bundles to assign. Its first stage learns small changes across multiple outcomes using relationships among treatments and outcomes. Its second stage narrows the assignment space and applies Lagrangian relaxation to a small set of global constraints, making the constrained decision problem more scalable.

Offline experiments report improvements over leading methods, and online A/B tests show a 0.5% increase in daily active users. The system is deployed on Kuaishou, which serves more than 100 million users daily. These findings connect the modeling contribution to an operational result: jointly considering notification choices and constraints can translate estimated small effects into measurable engagement gains at scale.
icml-2026-large-scale-notification-dispa.tldr: BUOPLR estimates the effects of notification timing-and-style bundles and assigns them under budgets and quotas, raising DAU by 0.5% in online tests.

paragraphs: Detecting watermarked text in a continuous stream creates a statistical challenge beyond evaluating a fixed collection of documents. Machine-generated passages may be rare and mixed with human writing. Repeatedly applying offline detectors can fail to control the online false discovery rate, the error measure this paper targets.

LORD-GoF combines a goodness-of-fit statistic with the LORD procedure for online testing. It dynamically adjusts detection thresholds as the stream progresses. The authors prove that this approach can keep the online false discovery rate below a level chosen by the user, giving the sequence of detection decisions an explicit statistical control.

Experiments use watermarked outputs from Qwen-2.5-3B, Sheared-LLaMA-2.7B, and OPT-1.3B with Gumbel-Max and Inverse Transform watermarking. The method maintains detection power comparable to offline benchmarks while controlling the online error measure in mixed streams. The findings indicate that adapting thresholds across successive tests can support useful watermark detection when the content arrives incrementally and watermarked material is sparse.
icml-2026-lord-gof-a-robust-online-detec.tldr: LORD-GoF dynamically adjusts watermark-detection thresholds to control online false discoveries in sparse streams mixed with human writing.

paragraphs: LoRA reduces fine-tuning costs by restricting model updates to a low-rank form. This paper examines whether ordinary matrix rank adequately describes the diversity of those updates. The authors argue that it misses duplicated directions and redundancy within the update subspace, leaving an important aspect of adaptation uncharacterized.

They propose using Kruskal rank as a more informative measure of update diversity and develop Low Kruskal Rank Adaptation, or LoKRA, around that analysis. The method comes with theoretical guarantees intended to address limitations of LoRA. An enhanced version, LoKRA+, provides a tighter theoretical lower bound on Kruskal rank.

Across multiple language models and benchmarks, the authors report that their methods consistently outperform LoRA and other baselines, with LoKRA+ delivering stronger empirical performance. The central contribution is a different way to analyze and construct parameter-efficient updates: the diversity of update directions becomes an explicit consideration alongside the familiar goal of keeping the number of trainable parameters small.
icml-2026-low-kruskal-rank-adaptation-5d.tldr: LoKRA uses Kruskal rank to address redundancy in parameter-efficient updates and reports improvements over LoRA across multiple language models.

paragraphs: Robotic manipulation combines broad movements with precise interactions where contact matters. Move-Then-Operate builds this distinction into a vision–language–action model. It separates coarse relocation from contact-critical operation so that the policy can learn the different dynamics associated with each phase of a manipulation task.

The architecture uses two experts and a learned selector that routes behavior between them. Training phase labels are generated automatically through a multimodal language-model pipeline using lightweight context, including end-effector velocity and subtask decomposition. This provides supervision intended to align the split with human motor patterns without treating the entire task as one undifferentiated behavior.

On RoboTwin2, the method achieves 68.9% average success and reports a +24% improvement over the monolithic π₀ baseline. It also matches or exceeds models trained on ten times more data and reaches peak performance in 40% fewer training steps. These results support phase-specific specialization as an effective architectural choice for efficient, high-precision manipulation in the reported evaluation.
icml-2026-move-then-operate-behavioral-p.tldr: Move-Then-Operate separates relocation and precise interaction into two learned experts, improving robotic manipulation success and training efficiency.

paragraphs: Triggerable watermarks help model owners verify ownership when another party extracts a model’s behavior. Many approaches require additional training, which makes them harder to introduce after deployment. Neural Honeytrace provides a plug-and-play alternative designed to embed a watermark without retraining the protected model.

The framework treats watermark transmission as an information problem and introduces a multi-step transmission strategy. It uses the long-tailed effect of backdoor learning to support efficient, robust embedding. This reframing focuses on how a watermark is transmitted through the extraction process, addressing a setting where the owner wants a recognizable signal to remain available for later ownership verification.

Experiments report that the average query count for worst-case, t-test-based ownership verification can fall to as little as 2% of that required by existing methods. The framework incurs zero training cost. These findings concern two practical costs of watermarking: introducing the ownership signal and gathering enough query evidence to verify it after extraction.
icml-2026-neural-honeytrace-plug-play-wa.tldr: Neural Honeytrace embeds ownership watermarks without retraining and substantially reduces verification queries in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Materials generation seeks many useful candidates that satisfy constraints, rather than a single correct response. PLaID++ adapts language-model post-training to this goal for crystal structures. The authors find that straightforward preference optimization with a coordinate-based representation causes mode collapse, undermining the desired diversity of generated candidates.

They introduce a compact text representation informed by crystal symmetry through Wyckoff information. Encoding symmetry directly provides physical structure for learning, improves computational efficiency, and encourages generalization. Post-training then guides generation toward desirable chemical regions while supporting both stability-focused and property-guided design.

PLaID++ generates structures that are thermodynamically stable, unique, and novel at a rate more than 50% higher than prior methods. The authors also find that training conditional and unconditional generation together benefits both tasks when data are scarce. These findings show why representation matters in scientific post-training: the format of a candidate can help align optimization with physical constraints while preserving the diversity that discovery requires.
icml-2026-plaid-a-preference-aligned-lan.tldr: PLaID++ combines preference-aligned post-training with symmetry-informed crystal text to improve the rate of stable, unique, and novel material generation.

paragraphs: Adversarial imitation learning can produce high-quality imitation but often requires substantial interaction with an environment. Initializing its policy through behavioral cloning is one proposed way to reduce that burden. This paper analyzes why policy pretraining alone can leave a major obstacle unresolved: error in the reward used to guide learning.

The authors identify reward error as the dominant source of suboptimality in their analysis of policy-only pretraining. They then develop a connection between expert policies and shaping rewards. That connection leads to CoPT-AIL, which uses a single behavioral-cloning procedure to pretrain both the policy and the reward, preparing both components for subsequent adversarial learning.

The paper proves an improved imitation-gap bound over standard adversarial imitation learning and presents this as the first theoretical guarantee of pretraining’s benefits in this setting. Experiments also report superior performance over existing methods. The contribution explains why a good initial policy may be insufficient and supplies a theoretically grounded way to initialize its accompanying learning signal.
icml-2026-provably-efficient-policy-rewa.tldr: CoPT-AIL jointly pretrains policy and reward through behavioral cloning, improving theoretical imitation bounds and reported performance.

paragraphs: Contextual optimization uses features about a situation to choose actions under uncertainty. In practice, historical features may be incomplete because data sources differ or collection is costly. This paper develops a decision-making method that works directly with those partial observations instead of first filling in a complete dataset.

The approach builds ambiguity sets: collections of candidate distributions compatible with the available evidence. It incorporates the general structure of how values become missing, keeping candidate distributions consistent with what was observed. Decisions are then chosen through distributionally robust optimization, so uncertainty from incomplete information enters the decision problem itself.

For settings with discrete or continuous features and outcomes, the authors derive tractable reformulations and finite-sample guarantees for performance on new data. Experiments report better out-of-sample performance and reliability than leading baselines, including impute-then-optimize approaches. The findings support integrating missing-data uncertainty into optimization rather than resolving it entirely in a separate preprocessing step before making decisions.
icml-2026-robust-contextual-optimization.tldr: The method makes robust contextual decisions directly from incomplete features by optimizing over distributions consistent with observed data and missingness structure.

paragraphs: Time-series foundation models can struggle with long forecasting horizons because processing extensive histories is computationally expensive. SPRINT addresses this at inference time without additional training. It performs part of the forecasting in a lower-resolution space, allowing the model to use a longer look-back window at reduced computational cost.

Downsampling can discard information and create a mismatch between input and output resolution. SPRINT handles this by separating the series into trend and seasonal components. It forecasts the low-frequency trend through a Resolution Interpolation workflow, while a Pattern Replication mechanism preserves high-frequency seasonal details. The two components therefore receive processing suited to their different temporal structure.

Experiments report a 19% accuracy improvement compared with leading time-series foundation models, alongside 6.4-fold lower maximum memory use and 16.9-fold shorter inference time. The results support a practical route to longer-context forecasting: simplify the slower-moving component while retaining a separate mechanism for recurring fine-scale patterns, all through an inference-time addition.
icml-2026-see-more-forecast-better-and-f.tldr: SPRINT separates trend and seasonality to enable training-free downsampled forecasting with longer context, improved accuracy, and lower inference costs.

paragraphs: The paper studies federated learning when clients have different data and encounter changing domains over a sequence of tasks, while the possible labels stay the same. Raw data cannot be shared, and only some clients participate in each training round. The aim is to learn through these changes while controlling damage to performance on earlier tasks.

The proposed algorithm, SPECIAL, modifies FedAvg at the server. Each round, the server combines updates from a uniformly sampled subset of clients, then blends that result with the previous global model through a proximal step. This previous model acts as an anchor that restrains accumulated drift. The method uses no replay buffers, synthetic data, or separate task heads, and keeps model size and communication cost unchanged.

The backward-transfer result bounds how much loss on earlier tasks can increase. Its drift-controlled bound shrinks with more rounds, local epochs, and participating clients. This provides a quantified guarantee about possible deterioration; it does not establish that every earlier task improves.

The convergence result applies uniformly across the task sequence for non-convex learning under partial participation. It gives an expected-gradient-norm rate of O(sqrt(E/(NT))), where E counts local epochs, T communication rounds, and N participating clients. The analysis distinguishes optimization variance from drift between tasks. Experiments on standard benchmarks support the theoretical findings.
icml-2026-server-proximal-aggregation-fo.tldr: SPECIAL anchors federated updates to the previous global model, bounding earlier-task deterioration and providing task-uniform convergence guarantees as domains change.

paragraphs: Software-engineering benchmarks often emphasize algorithmic exercises or Python bug fixing, leaving other developer activities less visible. SWE-Compass broadens evaluation by organizing different kinds of coding work within one framework. Its aim is to make assessment more representative of the variety of tasks encountered in real development workflows.

The benchmark contains 2,000 instances drawn from authentic GitHub pull requests and processed through systematic filtering and validation. It spans eight task types, eight programming scenarios, and ten languages. This structure supports examining where a model performs well or struggles across several dimensions of software engineering, rather than treating coding ability as one undifferentiated score.

The authors evaluate ten leading language models using SWE-Agent and Claude Code. Results reveal a clear hierarchy of difficulty across task types, languages, and scenarios. That variation is the central diagnostic finding: performance depends on which software-engineering activity is being tested. The authors hope the benchmark will provide a reproducible foundation for understanding and advancing agentic coding capabilities.
icml-2026-swe-compass-towards-unified-ev.tldr: SWE-Compass evaluates coding agents on 2,000 real pull-request tasks spanning eight task types, eight scenarios, and ten languages.

paragraphs: Forecasting methods often rely heavily on the latest observations. This paper identifies that tendency as recent-data bias and shows why it matters when recent measurements contain noise, missing values, or anomalies. If those observations dominate the prediction, a local disturbance can make the resulting forecast unreliable.

TameR seeks to reduce that dependence by making greater use of global context. A basis-aligned randomized sampling strategy reduces reliance on particular recent observations. A learnable periodicity extraction module, paired with a two-stage learning protocol, separates recurring patterns from the sampled residual components. Together, these elements organize historical information so that forecasting is less tied to the most recent data.

Across diverse perturbation scenarios, experiments report substantially greater robustness than leading methods while maintaining comparable accuracy on clean data. This combination matters because the goal is useful forecasting under corruption without sacrificing ordinary predictive quality. The findings support treating dependence on recent observations as a specific design issue that can be addressed through sampling and periodic structure.
icml-2026-taming-the-recent-data-bias-to.tldr: TameR combines randomized historical sampling and periodic-pattern extraction to make forecasts less vulnerable to corrupted recent observations.

paragraphs: The annealing stage of language-model pre-training is an important period for final convergence. This paper asks how training samples should be selected during that stage. It replaces selection heuristics with an optimization-based analysis of the loss landscape, focusing on how its curvature differs across directions.

The authors argue that optimal convergence requires gradient updates to meet different constraints along different eigen-directions. DiReCT translates that argument into a constrained sample-selection problem. It examines per-sample gradients through the spectral properties of the Hessian and selects samples whose updates satisfy the resulting directional constraints.

This makes the expected direction of a sample’s training update central to deciding whether to use it during annealing. The intended effect is to follow a curvature-aware descent path as the model converges. Experiments across different model scales report consistent state-of-the-art performance. These findings support the proposed connection between late-stage sample selection and optimization geometry, with data choice guided by the update behavior that the analysis calls for.
icml-2026-towards-efficient-llms-anneali.tldr: DiReCT selects annealing-stage training samples by constraining their gradients according to the curvature of the language model’s loss landscape.

paragraphs: This paper studies how uncertainty changes during chain-of-thought generation. It finds a recurring transition from an exploratory region to a confidence region, where answers become accurate and stable. Models often continue producing unnecessary tokens after that transition, creating an opportunity to reduce computation.

The authors frame detection of this transition as a sequential change-point problem and use the Cumulative Sum algorithm, or CUSUM, to monitor reasoning during inference. The framework requires no training. Its confidence signal can support early stopping or assign greater weight to converged trajectories when combining multiple generated answers.

For early exit, the reported configuration achieves 63.06% accuracy with an 11.1% reduction in tokens, outperforming DEER and Dynasor in accuracy. The authors report a better accuracy–computation trade-off, and CUSUM-weighted voting consistently outperforms self-consistency in their test-time-scaling experiments. These findings make the observed uncertainty transition useful as an inference-control signal, connecting a property of generated reasoning to decisions about when to stop or which answers to emphasize.
icml-2026-unveiling-the-entropy-dynamics.tldr: A training-free CUSUM detector identifies confidence transitions in chain-of-thought generation to improve early stopping and multi-answer voting.

paragraphs: Multimodal reasoning does not necessarily need the same visual information at every generation step. This paper finds that only a small subset of visual tokens is critical at a given step, and that the relevant subset changes during reasoning. A single pruning decision at the beginning cannot directly reflect that changing demand.

VisionPulse prunes visual tokens step by step. It uses a lightweight measure of visual attention mass, which the authors find strongly positively correlated with effective visual-token usage, to determine how many tokens to retain. It then keeps the most critical tokens within that budget. This also addresses redundant visual context that can pull reasoning toward irrelevant image regions.

Experiments report retaining only 5% of visual tokens per step while shortening reasoning traces by 11.2%, with accuracy almost unchanged. The findings connect two sources of inference overhead: excessive visual context and unnecessarily long reasoning. Dynamically selecting visual evidence can reduce both in the reported evaluations.
icml-2026-visionpulse-dynamic-visual-spa.tldr: VisionPulse dynamically retains a small, changing set of visual tokens during reasoning, reducing visual context and reasoning length with almost unchanged accuracy.
